card.name: Linking words in Unix permission tutorials
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as a comma, "to" or "when" in Unix and server access-control tutorials, just before a verb about allowing, reading, writing or protecting files.

modes.label: Infinitive "to" before an access verb
modes.description: The word "to" after want or need, ahead of verbs like allow, protect, read or write in file-permission text.
modes.example: But you want<< to>> allow just this particular file to be deleted

modes.label: Comma after a user name
modes.description: A comma following a named example user in a permissions scenario.
modes.example: imagine trying allow a single user, Bob<<,>> to read one of your files.

modes.label: Linking word in command descriptions
modes.description: A conjunction or verb in a short description of a command's behavior.
modes.example: batch - execute commands<< when>> the system load permits The batch utility
